jobs.prompt:
chore(cpp): integrate the repaired port head with the WebSocket, logging, CI, macOS, Pi packaging and operator branches (stage 2a)

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-suite-repair-20261118-44210723939-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: a known-good state of `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`), with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`), vendored simdjson and simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/`), and about 442 standalone test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). On this state the release build passes its whole suite on Linux ARM64. The native gateway is already 1.2-1.9x faster than the TypeScript gateway on Bun end to end and uses about a third of the memory (`cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-perf-request-path-20261117.md`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, an Apple Silicon Mac and a Raspberry Pi.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh ...`, the file lacks its executable bit), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy above wins). `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` and the vendored libraries link into every test.

About ten other agents are changing other parts of `cpp/gateway` on their own branches at the same time (URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, passkey CBOR and ASN.1, BigInt, date/console/filesystem/env/headers helpers, the stored-value reader, a test-suite repair). You are an INTEGRATOR (see TASK); keep your own edits to what integration needs.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.

OWNED PATHS
- anything under `cpp/gateway/` and `.github/workflows/cpp-gateway-*.yml` that the integration needs. Not the TypeScript; not vendored sources under `cpp/gateway/third_party/` (byte-identical to what the branches vendored).

TASK
You start from `agent-jobs/cppgw-suite-repair-20261118-44210723939-1`: the port head with the hand-written JSON parser deleted (simdjson only), simdutf encoding, the central input-limits header, a faster large-body path, a repaired CI workflow, and a suite that is green on ARM64 (report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-suite-repair-20261118.md`). Merge these reviewed and accepted branches into it with ordinary `git merge` commits, in this order (fetch each from `origin`):
  1. `agent-jobs/cppgw-ci-sanitizers-c1-44248514285-1`: unified CI workflow (release + sanitizer shards + robustness harnesses).
  2. `agent-jobs/cppgw-perf-log-records-c1-44248514285-1`: cheaper terminal log records (two application files).
  3. `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-websocket-c1-44248514285-1`: Boost.Beast for outbound WebSocket framing, masking, handshake tokens, UTF-8 validation.
  4. `agent-jobs/cppgw-macos-requal-20261118-44214118327-1`: macOS build script and guide (it was branched from an ICU-casing branch: that ICU change to `src/rt/string.cpp` is ALSO accepted, keep it).
  5. `agent-jobs/cppgw-pi-compat-20261118-44214118327-1`: portable ARM64 packaging and Raspberry Pi guide.
  6. `agent-jobs/cppgw-ops-side-by-side-c1-44248514285-1`: operator kit (docs, unit template, dry-run script).
  7. `agent-jobs/cppgw-keep-audit-c1-44248514285-1`: audit report and briefs (docs only).
Several of these were branched from older commits of the same line, so expect conflicts in shared registries (`fuzz/targets.json`, `docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `cmake/vendors.json`, `tests/LINKS.txt`, `docs/CI.md`) and in `src/rt/string.cpp` (ICU casing/collation from branch 4 versus simdutf UTF conversion on your base: keep BOTH: ICU for case mapping and collation, simdutf for UTF conversion). Resolve keeping each branch's intent; never resolve by dropping a branch's change. Then:
  a. Make every build path work (CMake, `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `cmake/vendors.json`, the portable CI driver `cmake/ci/driver.py`).
  b. CI follow-up: on GitHub's hosted ARM64 runner `tests/rt/sqlite_test.cpp` failed 3 of 29 cases because the driver linked the distribution SQLite instead of the pinned 3.54.0 that the workflow builds into `/usr/local` (the three cases pin version behaviour: text rendering of REAL 2^51 and opening a garbage file). Make the driver and workflow link the pinned SQLite explicitly (include and library paths, rpath) and print `sqlite3_libversion()` in the job log.
  c. Run the whole suite, release configuration, all shards, and the `asan` configuration for the components these branches touched, until everything is green on your ARM64 runner. A test that fails only because a merged branch intentionally changed behaviour under the owner policy gets its expectation updated with the reason in the commit message; a functional failure gets fixed.
Write `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-s2a-20261118.md`: merge order, each conflict and its resolution, test decisions, final counts per shard, first-party production lines in `src/rt` + `src/runtime` before and after.

DONE WHEN
`bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard N/4` passes for N = 1..4 with zero failing binaries on your ARM64 runner, `git log` shows the seven merges, and the report is complete. The maintainer will merge this stage with another integration stage next.
